html:
In the app

File → New Project… → A graded level → 7. Guided mode opens on this chapter: the tags, every rung below under its fold, a Verify check, and five results — pump A stops on its count and B tops up to HI, the batch heats with the mixer running, all three batches made, every batch on spec, under par.

No belt, no bottles. One Mix Tank (built after the LogixPro Batch Mix) and a console. Make three batches, one of each recipe, in the order the recipe selector shows: the level turns the selector to the next recipe each time a batch drains. Par 240 s.

The tank

Where the ingredients come from

Each inlet is piped to a Supply Tote: Supply_A holds water, Supply_B orange concentrate, 10,000 units each. The pipes are part of the scene. The Mix Tank’s Inlet A fed from and Inlet B fed from settings name the totes, and the pumps take what they move out of them. An empty tote runs its pump dry: no flow, no flowmeter pulses, and a line in the Simulator Log. An inlet fed from nothing is on the plant supply header, drawn in 3D as a riser out of the floor with a ball valve. The outlet, with nothing piped to it, runs to a floor drain.

The flowmeters are inline digital meters. The LCD shows the rate in units a second and the running total; the green lamp is on while liquid moves and the amber one blinks with each pulse the meter sends the controller. Tick Flowmeters also report their rate and each meter adds an analog input, FlowA_Rate and so on. Bind that signal to a REAL tag in its properties and the program reads 87.5, not 87. While the ingredients go in, the tank’s contents look clear and pale; mixing, faster when warm, turns them cloudy, and the next batch starts clear again.

The tank has a local panel on its shell, and the console side of the floor has a Process HMI on a pedestal, Tank_HMI. Both show the same live faceplate: the vessel with its level and probes, the temperature against the high limit, the mixing time, a one-minute trend, the ratio, the flows, which pumps and heater are on, the state and an alarm line. It is drawn the way plant HMIs are, grey with colour only for what is running or wrong, so a lit heater or an alarm stands out at a glance. The HMI reads the tank directly; it is a window for you, not an input to the program.

How each batch is scored

RecipeIngredient ATemperatureMix at least
A50 %150 °F10 s
B75 %130 °F15 s
C25 %170 °F8 s
Graded when the batch drainsPoints
A share within ±5 % of the recipe+100 (−50 if not)
Temperature when the outlet pump started: recipe −3 to +8 °F+100 (−50 if not)
Mixed at least the recipe time+100 (−50 if not)
Less than 80 % of the tank (a short batch)−50
Overflowed past the top−100
Scorched (heater on with the element uncovered)−100
Outlet pump ran dry more than 3 s−25
All three batches under par (240 s)+200

How to pass it, step by step

1. Think in steps, not in rungs. One DINT, Step, says what the tank is doing: 0 waiting for an empty

2. Read the recipe into tags. Three rungs: the selector position sets Target_A (pulses of A), Target_T

3. Dose A by counting. Pump A runs in step 1; a CTU counts Flow_A; at Target_A move to step 2.

4. Top up with B to HI. Pump B runs in step 2 until Hi_Level, and the HI probe ends it — B is "whatever

5. Heat with hysteresis. Latch Heat_On below the target minus 2 °F, unlatch it at the target. Gate the

6. Mix on a timer with a preset tag. TON(Mix_T,Mix_Pre,0) in step 3 — the preset operand can be a 7. Drain to empty. Pump_Out in step 4. The level reads 0 % with a few units still in the tank, so run the

Tags this lesson needs

The alias tags of the machine are made for you; create these before you type the rungs. Verify reports any you miss.

Run, recipe A and the start of a batch

The recipe rungs run every scan; the level only turns the selector when a batch has drained, so the values never change in the middle of one. Only recipe A is here: the first batch is always A, and the rungs for B and C come after the batch-out rung, where they can be seen working the moment they are written. SUB(Target_T,2,Target_Lo) is the bottom of the heater’s band. A batch starts only on an empty tank: XIO(Lo_Level) and LEQ(Tank_Level,0).

Dosing: A by count, B to HI

The CTU counts every rising edge of Flow_A, whatever step it is in — fine, because only step 1 runs pump A, and the batch start resets it.

Heating and mixing

Rung 12 unlatches Heat_On at the target, outside step 3, or at the high limit; rung 13 is the only rung that drives the heater, and it refuses an uncovered element. Rung 14 leaves step 3 when the mixing timer is done and the batch is at least at the bottom of its band.

Draining and counting

Recipes B and C

Written after batch A has drained, these go true as soon as the level turns the selector to B, and to C after the next batch.

Lamps

Run it

Load your program, Run mode, Start. Watch the display: FILLING with the A share climbing, then B pulling it down to the recipe; HEAT+MIX with the temperature climbing at a little over 2 °F a second; DRAINING; EMPTY; and the selector turns. The Simulator Log grades each batch as it drains. A run on 3 of 3 bottles in the right bin, nothing lost, in about 181 s against a par of 240 s: 1100 points and three stars.

Try It

The reference program wastes most of its time heating after the tank is full. Start the heater as soon as Lo_Level is covered — in step 1 — and watch two things happen: the batch is ready much sooner, and every slug of cold ingredient pulls the temperature down (the tank mixes it in), so the heater works against the fill. Beat 150 s. Then take XIC(Lo_Level) out of the heater rung and start a batch: the element comes on before the liquid covers it, and the batch is scorched. Last, give the heater no band at all — LES(Tank_Temp,Target_T)OTE(Heater) — and watch it chatter on and off at the setpoint in Monitor Tags.

Try it: run a tote dry

Set Supply_B’s Starts at to 15 % (1,500 units) and run the reference program. Batches 1 and 2 take about 1,350 units of B between them, so in batch 3 the tote empties while pump B is topping up. Pump B runs dry, the HI probe never makes, and the program sits in step 2 forever with the Run lamp on. A real line would be exactly as stuck. Make two fixes. First, a watchdog: XIC(Run)EQU(Step,2)TON(B_Fill_T,20000,0), and when it is done, light Lamp_Fault and stop. Second, use the tote’s own LowLevel switch, a digital input like any other (alias it as Tote_B_Low): do not start a batch while it is on. The watchdog catches the failure; the low switch stops you walking into it. In Run mode, clicking an empty tote swaps in a full one, the way a forklift would.

A mix tank on the bottle line

The Mix Tank pipes to a filler the way the Reservoir does: put one in place of Supply_Tank and pick it in the Filler’s Fed from, which lists every tote, tank, reservoir and mix tank in the scene. A Tank can also be fed from the Mix Tank (its Inlet fed from); it then fills only while the mix tank’s outlet pump runs and its own inlet valve is open. The filler then only gets product while the tank’s outlet pump runs, so the program has to make a batch first and then hold Pump_Out on while the filler draws — a batch-to-line handoff that a supply tank never asked for.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: RUN: the seal-in, from the console buttons or the START and STOP on the HMI touch screen

pred.q: Start_PB is on, HMI_Start is on, Run is off, Stop_PB is off, HMI_Stop is off and E_Stop is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Run is on.

rungs.words: When either (Start_PB (Start push button, momentary) is on), (HMI_Start (START on the Tank_HMI touch screen (pulsed by the HMI)) is on) or (Run (Seal-in run bit) is on), Stop_PB (Stop push button, momentary) is off, HMI_Stop (STOP on the Tank_HMI touch screen (pulsed by the HMI)) is off and E_Stop (E-stop, NC: 1 = healthy) is on, the rung turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Start_PB) Examine If Closed asks: true when Start_PB is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(HMI_Start) Examine If Closed asks: true when HMI_Start is on.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIO(Stop_PB) Examine If Open asks: true when Stop_PB is off.
  3. XIO(HMI_Stop) Examine If Open asks: true when HMI_Stop is off.
  4. XIC(E_Stop) Examine If Closed asks: true when E_Stop is on.
  5. OTE(Run) Output Energize does: turns Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

pats.why: The start condition turns Run on, and Run’s own contact in the parallel path keeps the rung true after the start goes away. Anything in series outside the branch (a stop, a fault) breaks it, and then it stays off until the start is made again.
pats.think: a doorbell button and a hand. The start button is the doorbell, pressed for a moment. The seal-in contact is a hand that grabs the circuit as soon as the output comes on and keeps holding after you let go. The stop button, in series, is the only thing that can knock that hand away.
pats.watch: The stop has to be in series outside the branch. Put it inside the start path only and the seal-in path bypasses it: the stop no longer stops.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: RECIPE A: 50 % A — 45 pulses of 20 units is 900 of the 1800 a full tank holds at the HI probe; 150 °F; mix 10 s
rungs.words: When Recipe_A (Recipe selector at A (left)) is on, the rung puts 45 into Target_A (Pulses of A for the selected recipe), puts 150 into Target_T (Temperature for the selected recipe, °F) and puts 10000 into Mix_Pre (Mixing time for the selected recipe, ms).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Recipe_A) Examine If Closed asks: true when Recipe_A is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(45,Target_A) Move does: puts 45 into Target_A. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(150,Target_T) Move does: puts 150 into Target_T. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(10000,Mix_Pre) Move does: puts 10000 into Mix_Pre. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: Hysteresis: heat on below the target minus 2 °F, off at the target
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung makes Target_Lo (Heater comes back on below this, °F) = Target_T (Temperature for the selected recipe, °F) − 2.
rungs.ltr: 1. SUB(Target_T,2,Target_Lo) Subtract does: makes Target_Lo = Target_T − 2. Every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: STEP 0 → 1: an empty tank and the line running: start a batch
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 0, Lo_Level (LO probe covered (10 %)) is off and Tank_Level (Tank level 0-100 %) is at most 0, the rung resets A_Count (Flowmeter A pulses this batch), resets Mix_T (Mixing time this batch) and puts 1 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,0) Equal asks: true when Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. XIO(Lo_Level) Examine If Open asks: true when Lo_Level is off.
  4. LEQ(Tank_Level,0) Less Than or Equal asks: true when Tank_Level is at most 0.
  5. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. RES(A_Count) Reset does: resets A_Count. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 2
    1. RES(Mix_T) Reset does: resets Mix_T. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 3
    1. MOV(1,Step) Move does: puts 1 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 0, to 1); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.
pats.think: a recipe card with numbered steps and one finger on it. Each rung only reads the line under the finger; when its line is done it moves the finger to the next number.
pats.watch: A rung further down that tests for the new step number sees it in this same scan. Rung order decides whether the next step starts now or next scan.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: STEP 1: dose ingredient A

pred.q: Run is off and Step is 1. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Pump_A is off. It stops at XIC(Run).

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 1, the rung turns Pump_A (Ingredient A pump) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,1) Equal asks: true when Step equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. OTE(Pump_A) Output Energize does: turns Pump_A on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: Count flowmeter A: one count per rising edge, one edge per 20 units
rungs.words: When Flow_A (Flowmeter A pulses (20 units each)) is on, the rung counts A_Count (Flowmeter A pulses this batch) up by one (preset 9999).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Flow_A) Examine If Closed asks: true when Flow_A is on.
  2. CTU(A_Count,9999,0) Count Up does: counts A_Count up by one (preset 9999). It counts false-to-true transitions of the rung, not scans; .DN is on once the count reaches the preset.

pats.t: A counter: one count per false-to-true.
pats.why: A_Count counts transitions of the rung, not scans, so a part that sits in front of an eye for a second counts once.
pats.think: a clicker at a door: one click per person coming in, however slowly they walk through.
pats.watch: A counter keeps its count until a RES. If the count should start again at each batch, something has to reset it.

rungs.head: Rung 6
rungs.comment: A dosed: on to B

pred.q: Step is 1, A_Count.ACC is 38 and Target_A is 29. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 1 and A_Count.ACC (the accumulated value of A_Count: Flowmeter A pulses this batch) is at least Target_A (Pulses of A for the selected recipe), the rung puts 2 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,1) Equal asks: true when Step equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. GEQ(A_Count.ACC,Target_A) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when A_Count.ACC is at least Target_A.
  3. MOV(2,Step) Move does: puts 2 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 1, to 2); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 7
rungs.comment: STEP 2: top up with ingredient B to the HI probe
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 2 and Hi_Level (HI probe covered (90 %)) is off, the rung turns Pump_B (Ingredient B pump) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,2) Equal asks: true when Step equals 2. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. XIO(Hi_Level) Examine If Open asks: true when Hi_Level is off.
  4. OTE(Pump_B) Output Energize does: turns Pump_B on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 8
rungs.comment: Full: heat and mix

pred.q: Hi_Level is off and Step is 2. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Step is not written (it keeps its value). It stops at XIC(Hi_Level).

rungs.words: When Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 2 and Hi_Level (HI probe covered (90 %)) is on, the rung puts 3 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,2) Equal asks: true when Step equals 2. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Hi_Level) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hi_Level is on.
  3. MOV(3,Step) Move does: puts 3 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 2, to 3); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 9
rungs.comment: STEP 3: mix
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 3, the rung turns Mixer (Mixer motor) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,3) Equal asks: true when Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. OTE(Mixer) Output Energize does: turns Mixer on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 10
rungs.comment: Mixing time: the preset is a tag the recipe rung sets

pred.q: Run is on and Step is 3. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Mix_T times toward its preset.

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 3, the rung runs the timer Mix_T (Mixing time this batch) toward Mix_Pre.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,3) Equal asks: true when Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. TON(Mix_T,Mix_Pre,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Mix_T toward Mix_Pre. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Mix_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Rung 11
rungs.comment: HEATER with hysteresis: on below the target minus 2
rungs.words: When Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 3 and Tank_Temp (Tank temperature, °F) is less than Target_Lo (Heater comes back on below this, °F), the rung latches Heat_On (Heater wanted (with hysteresis)) on.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,3) Equal asks: true when Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. LES(Tank_Temp,Target_Lo) Less Than asks: true when Tank_Temp is less than Target_Lo.
  3. OTL(Heat_On) Output Latch does: latches Heat_On on. It only ever sets the bit; the bit stays on after the rung goes false.

pats.why: Heat_On stays on after this rung goes false; only an OTU somewhere else turns it off. Read the program for that OTU before you trust the bit.
pats.think: a light switch rather than a doorbell: flick it on and it stays on until someone flicks it off.
pats.watch: A latched bit survives a stop, and it survives a download that keeps tag values. If nothing ever unlatches it, the machine remembers a state that is long gone.

rungs.head: Rung 12
rungs.comment: off at the target, outside step 3, or at the high limit

pred.q: Thermostat is off, Tank_Temp is 42, Target_T is 48 and Step is 3. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Heat_On is left as it was. None of the branch’s paths is true.

rungs.words: When either (Tank_Temp (Tank temperature, °F) is at least Target_T (Temperature for the selected recipe, °F)), (Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) is not 3) or (Thermostat (High-limit thermostat, closes at 180 °F) is on), the rung unlatches Heat_On (Heater wanted (with hysteresis)).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 3 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. GEQ(Tank_Temp,Target_T) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Tank_Temp is at least Target_T.
    Path 2
    1. NEQ(Step,3) Not Equal asks: true when Step is not 3.
    Path 3
    1. XIC(Thermostat) Examine If Closed asks: true when Thermostat is on.
  2. OTU(Heat_On) Output Unlatch does: unlatches Heat_On. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears Heat_On when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Rung 13
rungs.comment: Never heat an uncovered element (Lo_Level) or past the high-limit thermostat
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, Heat_On (Heater wanted (with hysteresis)) is on, Lo_Level (LO probe covered (10 %)) is on and Thermostat (High-limit thermostat, closes at 180 °F) is off, the rung turns Heater (Heater element) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. XIC(Heat_On) Examine If Closed asks: true when Heat_On is on.
  3. XIC(Lo_Level) Examine If Closed asks: true when Lo_Level is on.
  4. XIO(Thermostat) Examine If Open asks: true when Thermostat is off.
  5. OTE(Heater) Output Energize does: turns Heater on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 14
rungs.comment: Mixed long enough and at temperature: drain

pred.q: Mix_T.DN is on, Step is 3, Tank_Temp is 28 and Target_Lo is 22. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 3, Mix_T.DN (the done bit of Mix_T: Mixing time this batch) is on and Tank_Temp (Tank temperature, °F) is at least Target_Lo (Heater comes back on below this, °F), the rung puts 4 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,3) Equal asks: true when Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(Mix_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mix_T.DN is on.
  3. GEQ(Tank_Temp,Target_Lo) Greater Than or Equal asks: true when Tank_Temp is at least Target_Lo.
  4. MOV(4,Step) Move does: puts 4 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 3, to 4); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Rung 15
rungs.comment: STEP 4: drain
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 4, the rung turns Pump_Out (Outlet pump) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,4) Equal asks: true when Step equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. OTE(Pump_Out) Output Energize does: turns Pump_Out on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 16
rungs.comment: The level reads 0 with a few units left: run the pump on a second

pred.q: Step is 5 and Tank_Level is 0. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Empty_T is reset to 0. It stops at EQU(Step,4).

rungs.words: When Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 4 and Tank_Level (Tank level 0-100 %) is at most 0, the rung runs the timer Empty_T (Run the outlet pump on a moment after the level reads 0) toward 1000 ms (1 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,4) Equal asks: true when Step equals 4. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. LEQ(Tank_Level,0) Less Than or Equal asks: true when Tank_Level is at most 0.
  3. TON(Empty_T,1000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer Empty_T toward 1000 ms (1 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: Empty_T counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Rung 17
rungs.comment: Batch out: count it, back to step 0
rungs.words: When Empty_T.DN (the done bit of Empty_T: Run the outlet pump on a moment after the level reads 0) is on and this is the first scan of it, the rung makes Batch_Count (Batches made: the BATCHES display) = Batch_Count + 1 and puts 0 into Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Empty_T.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when Empty_T.DN is on.
  2. ONS(Done_ONS) One Shot asks: true on the first scan its input is true (remembered in Done_ONS). It passes power for one scan only, the scan its input goes from false to true; its storage bit remembers last scan.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. ADD(Batch_Count,1,Batch_Count) Add does: makes Batch_Count = Batch_Count + 1. Every scan the rung is true; behind a one-shot it adds once per event.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(0,Step) Move does: puts 0 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.t: One-shot: once per event, not once per scan.
pats.why: The rung after the one-shot is true for exactly one scan each time its conditions become true, so what follows happens once per event rather than every 20 ms while the condition lasts.
pats.think: a turnstile. However long you stand in it, it counts you once.
pats.watch: Each one-shot needs its own storage bit. Two one-shots sharing a bit fight over it, and one of them never fires.

rungs.head: Rung 18
rungs.comment: RECIPE B, after batch A (the level turns the selector to the middle when a batch is out): 75 % A — 68 pulses; 130 °F; mix 15 s

pred.q: Recipe_A is off and Recipe_C is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Target_A is written, Target_T is written and Mix_Pre is written.

rungs.words: When Recipe_A (Recipe selector at A (left)) is off and Recipe_C (Recipe selector at C (right); neither = B) is off, the rung puts 68 into Target_A (Pulses of A for the selected recipe), puts 130 into Target_T (Temperature for the selected recipe, °F) and puts 15000 into Mix_Pre (Mixing time for the selected recipe, ms).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Recipe_A) Examine If Open asks: true when Recipe_A is off.
  2. XIO(Recipe_C) Examine If Open asks: true when Recipe_C is off.
  3. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(68,Target_A) Move does: puts 68 into Target_A. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(130,Target_T) Move does: puts 130 into Target_T. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(15000,Mix_Pre) Move does: puts 15000 into Mix_Pre. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 19
rungs.comment: RECIPE C, after batch B: 25 % A — 23 pulses; 170 °F; mix 8 s
rungs.words: When Recipe_C (Recipe selector at C (right); neither = B) is on, the rung puts 23 into Target_A (Pulses of A for the selected recipe), puts 170 into Target_T (Temperature for the selected recipe, °F) and puts 8000 into Mix_Pre (Mixing time for the selected recipe, ms).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Recipe_C) Examine If Closed asks: true when Recipe_C is on.
  2. A branch of 3 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(23,Target_A) Move does: puts 23 into Target_A. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. MOV(170,Target_T) Move does: puts 170 into Target_T. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 3
    1. MOV(8000,Mix_Pre) Move does: puts 8000 into Mix_Pre. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Rung 20

pred.q: Run is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lamp_Run is off. It stops at XIC(Run).

rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Run (Run lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Run) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 21
rungs.words: When Run (Seal-in run bit) is on and Step (Batch step: 0 wait for an empty tank, 1 dose A, 2 top up with B, 3 heat and mix, 4 drain) equals 0, the rung turns Lamp_Idle (Idle lamp: waiting for an empty tank or a Start) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Run) Examine If Closed asks: true when Run is on.
  2. EQU(Step,0) Equal asks: true when Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  3. OTE(Lamp_Idle) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Idle on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 22

pred.q: Hi_Level is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Lamp_Full is on.

rungs.words: When Hi_Level (HI probe covered (90 %)) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Full (Full lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Hi_Level) Examine If Closed asks: true when Hi_Level is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Full) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Full on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Rung 23
rungs.comment: The fault lamp: the high-limit thermostat is made
rungs.words: When Thermostat (High-limit thermostat, closes at 180 °F) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Fault (Fault lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Thermostat) Examine If Closed asks: true when Thermostat is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.
